about: Gold set for my_kb/: NIST SP 800-63B-4 and CISA guidance on passwords and multifactor authentication. 6 questions the documents answer (each with an evidence phrase copied word-for-word from its source file) and 2 they do not.

questions.question: How long does a password have to be if it is the only thing a user types to log in?
evidence: a minimum of 15 characters in length

questions.question: Should our company force employees to change their passwords every 90 days?
evidence: SHALL NOT require subscribers to change passwords periodically

questions.question: How should a website store user passwords so they stay safe if the database is stolen?
evidence: Passwords SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable password hashing scheme

questions.question: How many failed login attempts in a row are allowed before the authenticator must be disabled?
evidence: no more than 100 by disabling that authenticator

questions.question: Which kind of MFA can actually stop a phishing attack?
evidence: The only widely available phishing-resistant authentication is FIDO/WebAuthn

questions.question: How does number matching stop an attacker from push-bombing a user into approving a login?
evidence: forces the user to enter numbers from the identity platform into their app

questions.question: What is a good recipe for chocolate chip cookies?
questions.note: Off-topic: nothing to do with authentication.

questions.question: How long can a session stay active before NIST requires the user to reauthenticate?
questions.note: Sounds right but is absent: NIST SP 800-63B-4 does set reauthentication timeouts (Sections 2.1.3, 2.2.3, 2.3.3 and 5.2), but none of that text is in my_kb/. The documents talk about NIST, authenticators and AAL levels, so retrieval finds close-looking chunks that do not contain the answer.
